nothing enters or leaves the reaction.

misconceptions.wrong: A reversible reaction goes one way then stops.
misconceptions.right: Both directions happen at the same time.

misconceptions.wrong: If forward is exothermic, so is backward.
misconceptions.right: The backward reaction is endothermic by the same amount.
They settle at an equilibrium below 100%.

infoPanels.title: ENERGY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
workedSteps: The ⇌ symbol shows a reversible reaction.

questions.text: State what the ⇌ symbol means in an equation. [1 mark]
The forward reaction is exothermic. State the energy change of the backward reaction and why. [2 marks]
Describe the colour change when hydrated copper sulfate is heated. [2 marks]
Explain why a reversible reaction does not give a 100% yield. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: If the forward reaction is ______, the backward reaction is ______.

questions.text: Suggest how copper sulfate could be used to test for water. [2 marks]

footer.tip: In a reversible reaction the energy change is equal and opposite each way.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why must a reversible reaction be in a closed system to reach equilibrium?
